purpose: Oritavancin is an antibiotic used to treat serious skin and skin structure infections caused by certain bacteria, including MRSA (a tough-to-treat staph infection). It works against gram-positive bacteria that can cause painful, swollen, or infected skin. Your doctor may prescribe this when other antibiotics are not the best option.
how_it_works: This medication works by attacking the bacterial cell wall, which is like the protective outer shell that bacteria need to survive. It actually hits the bacteria in three different ways at once, making it very hard for the germs to survive or become resistant. Think of it as a triple-action shield that breaks down the bacteria from multiple angles.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, and reactions at the infusion site such as redness, swelling, or irritation. Some people may also notice flushing or a rash during or after the infusion.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to vancomycin or any other antibiotics, as there may be a cross-reaction. This medication can interfere with certain blood clotting tests for up to 48 hours after your dose, so remind any healthcare provider you see. Avoid taking this drug if you have used unfractionated heparin within 48 hours. If you develop severe diarrhea, stop and contact your doctor, as it could signal a serious gut infection called C. diff.
typical_dosing: Oritavancin is given as a single one-time intravenous (IV) infusion of 1200 mg over 3 hours, usually in a hospital, clinic, or infusion center. One dose is often all that is needed, which is a big advantage over antibiotics taken daily for weeks.
